items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: Right down the street, a White fellow had a store named Mister Mack. And his kids were beautiful, you know. And he taught respect for everybody in the neighborhood.

ctx.x: In fact, I've got a thing that I wrote called "Hard Times In '29" that I'm going to get somebody to record one of these days, you know... But I remember all of these things that went down.

But getting back to the kids... It was really very strange. Right down the street, a White fellow had a store named Mister Mack. And his kids were beautiful, you know. And he taught respect for everybody in the neighborhood. No problems, you know. But there were just certain places you'd go, you'd run into it, and there you go -- you got to deal with it. You know, you'd have to deal with it.
